correctness.rationale: Each length-n output word labels exactly a path of n edges in an 8-vertex de Bruijn graph, and its determininized 256-state subset transition reaches empty if and only if the word is absent. Full BFS finds the exact earliest obstruction or proves surjectivity by compactness; this equivalence holds for arbitrary n. Two separately written exhaustive programs enumerated every one of 65,536 16-bit local rules and agreed on every histogram count and all four length-18 maximizers. The Python checker additionally verified zero absent at n=17 and exactly eight absent at n=18 for each extremal rule, independently tested output language membership against direct input-block enumeration, and checked the two explicit 18-symbol witnesses. No finite test is used to infer an unproved infinite statement.

value.rationale: For one-dimensional binary rules, four consecutive input positions are the first neighborhood size with surjective nonpermutive rules (Fukś–Skelton), making this the natural next full census beyond the elementary 256-rule case. The exact uniform 18-block surjectivity certificate and complete first-obstruction distribution distinguish hard-to-detect non-surjective maps and expose a genuine missing length-15 stratum. This resolves a natural finite classification invariant, not an arbitrary chosen rule slice or mere re-counting of the old 582 surjective rules.
